newsitem.title: USA: Capitol sees Q4 loss, but 98 profitability.
newsitem.headline: Capitol sees Q4 loss, but 98 profitability.

text.p: Capitol Multimedia Inc said Wednesday that it should be profitable in fiscal 1998 after acquiring a privately held developer and integrator of supply chain management software based in Dedham, Massachusettes.

Earlier this week, the company bought Client Server Technologies Inc for $4.2 million, consisting of $1.17 in cash, 1.2 million shares of Capitol Multimedia unregistered common stock and notes payable beginning in fiscal 1999.

"We've been in the multimedia business, and our stock has really been depressed, like all in the business. Now we've moved into the supply chain management software industry," said company chief financial officer Ed Terino.
Terino said the acquisition should boost revenues and make the company profitable in fiscal 1998.
"It'll probably increase our revenues by about $5 million a year in fiscal 1998, and it's also going to allow us be profitable," Terino said.
Capitol Multimedia shares closed at 1-7/8 Wednesday, up 5/16. The stock had been as low as 7/8 a week ago Wednesday, Terino said.
Terino said Capitol Multimedia expects to report a loss for the fourth quarter. First Call estimates were not immediately available.
Capitol Multimedia said Client Server Technologies had 1996 sales of about $3.7 million and a positive cash flow of about $500,000.

Capitol Multimedia, based in Concord, Massachusettes, had sales of nearly $1.9 million for the nine months ending December 31, 1996, down from sales of nearly $3.5 million in the 1995 nine-month period.
